items.a: As this year’s host of APEC, China stands ready to work with all parties for fruitful outcomes of the APEC “China Year,” and contribute to the economic growth in the Asia Pacific and beyond. For your question, I have no information to share at the moment.

items.a: China’s high-quality development is creating growth opportunities for the world. China is home to 25 of the world’s top 100 innovation clusters, and its scientific innovation has given more countries access to cutting-edge technologies and products at affordable prices, providing “digital ladders” for all countries. With the country’s installed capacity of photovoltaic power for the first time surpassing that of coal-fired power, China’s green transformation is making significant contributions to the global response to climate change

items.a: The possession of nuclear weapons is not an issue that Japan can “allow discussion” if it wants to. Japan is a non-nuclear-weapon state party to the Non-Proliferation Treaty and therefore has a bounden duty under international law to not receive, manufacture, acquire or transfer nuclear weapons. There is no room for negotiation. Just last February, Sanae Takaichi reiterated Japan’s commitment to the three non-nuclear principles. Japan’s representative reaffirmed multiple times at the Review Conference of the Parties to the NPT in May

items.a: I’d refer you to China’s competent authorities for the specific question. Let me say more broadly that we hope Europe will work with China in the same direction, resolve respective concerns through dialogue and consultation, and promote the sound and steady development of China-Europe economic and trade relations. We believe this serves the common interests of both sides. items.a: I would refer you to China’s competent authorities for anything specific. China always believes that it serves the shared interests of China and the EU to stay committed to openness and cooperation, and resolve economic and trade disputes through equal-footed dialogue and consultation.

items.a: For diehard supporters of “Taiwan independence” separatist forces, China will take all necessary punitive measures to firmly safeguard national sovereignty and territorial integrity. items.q: South Korea’s military said that North Korea on Monday fired multiple ballistic missiles off its east coast. I wonder if the foreign ministry has a comment on this.
items.a: We notice relevant reports, and have no comment to add.

items.q: A fresh Houthis strike hit Riyadh’s international airport on Sunday, killing one person and wounding 11 others. This comes a day after another deadly attack claimed by the Yemeni group. Can the Chinese foreign ministry comment on this?
items.a: China condemns the attacks, which caused significant casualties, and expresses grave concern over the escalating conflict. China opposes attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure. We urge the parties concerned to refrain from actions that could further escalate regional tensions, resolve differences and disputes through dialogue and negotiations, and work toward peace and stability in the region at an early date.

items.q: There was a landslide in Nepal’s Gorkha district that led to the downstream flooding in the Budhi Gandaki river. This area is part of a major trekking route. Were there any Chinese nationals affected by the flood?
items.a: We have no information on Chinese casualties for the time being. We extend sympathies to Nepal, and will provide assistance within our capacity in light of Nepal’s need.

items.q: The United States on Friday imposed sanctions on the International Criminal Court, vowing to cripple its operations just hours after the Nobel Peace Prize went to a former ICC judge. I wonder if China has a comment on this.
items.a: We noticed the developments. China is not a state party to the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court. China’s position on relevant issues is consistent.

items.a: I’m not familiar with the specifics. Let me say that China firmly opposes and combats hacking activities in accordance with the law. That said, we reject vilification against China under the pretext of cybersecurity.

items.q: It’s reported that Professor Colin Mackerras, renowned Australian sinologist who received the Chinese Government Friendship Award, passed away a few days ago after illness. Do you have any comment?
items.a: Professor Colin Mackerras was long committed to the friendly ties between Australia and China, and made important contribution to enhancing mutual understanding and friendship between the Chinese and Australian people. items.a: China has made clear its position on this issue more than once. We will continue working with relevant countries and the international community to make constructive efforts for restoring peace, stability and development in the Middle East.

China will keep its door wide open, and foster closer people-to-people bonds, so that more foreign friends can feel the pulse of China and fall in love with China.

items.q: Indian finance minister said today that India is facing growing trade imbalances with China and blamed China’s non-tariff barriers as a reason why this trade deficit is widening. Can you respond?
items.a: I’d refer you to China’s competent authorities for the specific question. What I can tell you is that China never aims for trade surplus. We stand ready to work with India to address each other’s economic and trade concerns in a balanced way and promote the steady development of bilateral relations.

items.a: As a WWII defeated nation and a non-nuclear-weapon state party to the Non-Proliferation Treaty, Japan is obligated under international law to refrain from breaching the exclusively defense-oriented policy and possessing nuclear weapons. It is high time that Japanese politicians caught up on history and law.

items.a: To improve and develop China-Philippines relations serves the interest of both sides. We firmly oppose certain Philippine individuals maliciously lashing out at China and hurting bilateral ties. The Philippine side should rein in such irresponsible behavior of those politicians.

The U.S. should abide by the principles of market economy, stop disrupting normal business cooperation, and help keep global industrial and supply chains stable through concrete actions. China will closely follow relevant developments and take necessary measures to safeguard its legitimate and lawful rights and interests.

items.a: China strictly abides by the relevant agreements and common understandings reached between the two countries, and conducts normal border patrol and control activities to safeguard its territorial sovereignty and stability in the border areas. items.a: We reject vilification and smears against Confucius Institute. Educational exchange and cooperation between China and the U.S. help enhance mutual understanding between the peoples of the two countries. They are desired by both sides and benefit both sides and should not be held back or disrupted.

items.a: China respects the choice of the Brazilian people.

items.a: China takes note of the announcement by Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court of President Lula’s runoff victory and extends congratulations on that. China stands ready to work with Brazil to advance the building of the China-Brazil community with a shared future.

items.a: As a major platform for international economic cooperation, the G20 plays an important role in strengthening multilateralism, promoting world economic growth, and improving global governance. South Africa is an important member of the G20. China supports South Africa in continuing its participation in G20 activities.
